title.narrative: Towards resilient communities based on nature-based sustainable livelihoods – supporting local indigenous communities in East Rennell, the only natural World Heritage site in the Pacific on the List of World Heritage in Danger

description.narrative:
The project aims to build capacities of indigenous local communities in the East Rennell World Heritage site in Solomon Islands, inscribed on the List of World Heritage in Danger in 2013, through developing nature-based sustainable livelihoods, to create an enabling environment for the local communities in East Rennell, the custodians of the World Heritage site, to achieve both conservation and sustainable development by fulfilling their basic needs and building resilience against socio-economic, cultural and environmental challenges that they are currently facing in a fully participatory manner. To this end, expertise from UNESCO and experts who have extensive experiences in supporting community development in the Pacific will be mobilized to help establish nature-based sustainable livelihoods integrating disaster risk reduction.
This will not only build resilience of communities affected by disasters and climate change, but it will also help developing positive perceptions and behavioural changes among the custodians of the World Heritage site to support nature-based solutions to counter destructive activities such as commercial logging and mining, while creating an enabling environment to achieve the Desired state of conservation for the removal of the property from the List of World Heritage in Danger by 2025 through enhancing well-being of the communities and fulfilling both heritage conservation and sustainable development.
